justification: The assessment uses exactly the reference deleted Tychonoff plank. The ambient space is compact Hausdorff, hence normal, and A and B are disjoint closed subsets of Y. Countably many row bounds have supremum α<ω₁, so any open U containing A contains (α+1,n) for every finite n. Any open V containing B contains these points for sufficiently large n. Thus disjoint open neighbourhoods are impossible.
